report.summary: 6 files modified under exporters/**, 4 test files modified under tests/test_*.py and tests/page.test.mjs, 1 file modified under site/**. 22 tests added (test_derive.py, test_export_sessions.py, test_export_board.py) plus 2 page checks strengthened; 4 pre-existing test assertions updated to match the corrected contract (cr() fixture gains hasFindingsBlock, two refresh.py write-count constants bumped for the new findings tab, FindingsOf assertions changed from [] to None where the fix requires it). All three configured suites green: python -m unittest discover -s tests 334 passed / 0 failed; node tests/page.test.mjs 99 passed / 0 failed; python -m unittest discover -s local/tests 194 passed / 0 failed (unchanged, per instruction, since local/** was not touched). Nothing committed, staged, pushed or deployed.

changes.why: CR-011-1 (HIGH): bump PARSER_VERSION 5->6 so every cached session is re-derived now that derive.py's rows carry a findings field parser 5 never wrote, closing the wrongly-resolved-findings path. CR-011-4 (MEDIUM): this exporter now owns its own projectTabs/<pid>.findings.json document's whole lifecycle (write and delete) instead of relying on export_board.py's folder wipe, so the document survives whichever exporter runs, in whichever order, or alone.

CR-011-4 (MEDIUM): the folder wipe now removes only the five tabs this exporter owns (TABS), never a document another exporter wrote (export_sessions.py's <pid>.findings.json); corrected the module docstring's claim that the whole folder is replaced.

CR-011-3 (MEDIUM): FENCE_JSON now matches the LAST fenced JSON block (tries every fence opening, keeps the rightmost one whose greedy body reaches the end of the text) instead of the leftmost-greedy match that let an earlier decoy fence swallow the real findings block. CR-011-2 (MEDIUM): findings_of() now returns None (no parseable block) as distinct from [] (a block that reported nothing); agent_row() records hasFindingsBlock; findings_doc() takes its authoritative latest-round ids only from the most recent round that actually carried a block, so a NO-GO round with no JSON (this repo's own findings-to-a-file workflow) never wrongly resolves open findings. CR-011-5 (MEDIUM): each finding in findings_doc() now carries round (1-based, first seen) and lastSeen (1-based, most recently seen). CR-011-8 (LOW, as noted): a finding with no id is dropped rather than collapsing every id-less finding into one entry.
CR-011-7 (LOW, as noted): added findings to TABS so a project whose only change is its findings ledger still moves its status document's updatedAt; noted the two-writer arrangement in the comment.

CR-011-5 (MEDIUM): the findings ledger now shows each finding's round attribution (a Round column: 'Round N' or 'Round first-last' when it has been seen again since), reading the round/lastSeen fields derive.py now publishes.

Drives and pins CR-011-2, CR-011-3, CR-011-5 and CR-011-8 at the derive.py unit level: a decoy-fence test, a None-vs-empty-list contract for findings_of(), a NO-GO-round-with-no-block test and a round-attribution test for findings_doc(), and an id-less-finding-is-dropped test. Updated the cr() fixture and the FindingsOf assertions that predated the corrected None/[] contract.

Drives and pins CR-011-1 (a cache written under the previous PARSER_VERSION, with findings stripped, is not reused), CR-011-2 (a real NO-GO round with no JSON block does not resolve F1), CR-011-4 (an Ownership class: export_board.py alone does not delete the findings document; running the exporters in refresh.py's order leaves exactly one; a project that loses its only round has its stale document removed), CR-011-5 (round/lastSeen on published findings) and CR-011-8 (a review naming two PBIs credits both ledgers).
Pins CR-011-4 from export_board.py's own side: a document outside TABS (a pre-planted <pid>.findings.json) survives a run of export_board.py alone, for both a still-configured and a dropped project.

Updated two pre-existing fixture-driven write/state counts (14 sets not 13, 16 committed state entries not 15) that shift because Out()'s fixture now creates one more tab per rf.TABS entry now that findings joined refresh.TABS (CR-011-7); no assertion was weakened, only the count corrected to the new, larger TABS tuple.
Pins CR-011-5 on the page: a finding shows 'Round 1' when raised and resolved in the same round, and 'Round 1-2' when still open since an earlier round.
